newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Opposition threatens to scuttle Hasina's rule.
newsitem.headline: Opposition threatens to scuttle Hasina's rule.

text.p: The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) threatened on Thursday to bring down the three-and-a-half month old government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, accusing it of falsehood and selfishness.
"The BNP is watching every move of the ruling Awami League, and crafting its own plan accordingly," a prominent BNP leader said, asking not to be identified. "We are preparing a fitting response."

The official's remarks echoed earlier warnings by the BNP's Secretary-General, Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan, that his party would "first protest, then resist and eventually launch a movement to bring down Hasina's government".

Her first 100 days in office, marked on Monday, had been an "era of falsehood, terrorism and politicisation of the administration," Bhuiyan said on Wednesday. Hasina marked the anniversary with a live television appearance on Tuesday night in which she blamed the former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia's BNP for the turmoil Bangladeshis have suffered in recent years.

She said her Awami League government, which took office on June 23 following an internationally-supervised election held under a neutral caretaker government, would do everything to mitigate people's sufferings and ensure rapid industrialisation and economic development.
Hasina reiterated her plan to buy electricity from India, if necessary, to overcome acute power shortages and encourage foreign investment. Her plan drew Bhuiyan's ire.
"We are absolutely opposed to importing power from India," Bhuiyan said.
He said Bangladesh's economic slowdown in recent years was a result of the Awami League's repeated calls for strikes in its bid to topple Khaleda Zia and had paralysed the country
"Now that Hasina is in the saddle she is trying to shift all the blame on us," one BNP leader said on Thursday.
"People will understand her selfish motives and her dirty tricks very soon," Bhuiyan said.

Awami leaders said they were not overly concerned by the BNP's threats. "People are aware of the BNP's misdeeds... Moreover, it is trying to depose a government elected in the country's fairest ever elections," one said.
"Let them growl, we will not go beating around the bushes. We have more serious jobs to do," he said.
